entry.title: Idira Privilege Cloud
entry.summary: Idira Privilege Cloud (Palo Alto Networks, formerly CyberArk Privilege Cloud) is an enterprise privileged access management SaaS platform. It secures credentials, controls access to privileged accounts, and audits access across hybrid and cloud infrastructures.Versions: 8.0.0 P10
entry.content:
Idira Privilege Cloud (Palo Alto Networks, formerly CyberArk Privilege Cloud) is an enterprise privileged access management SaaS platform. It secures credentials, controls access to privileged accounts, and audits access across hybrid and cloud infrastructures.

Versions: 8.0.0 P10

Introduction​

This plugin integrates RSA Governance & Lifecycle (G&L) with Idira Privilege Cloud (Palo Alto Networks Idira, formerly CyberArk Privilege Cloud). It retrieves managed credentials for collectors and connectors using Idira Identity OAuth 2.0 client credentials and the Privilege Cloud PVWA REST API.

Credentials are not cached; each collection or connector execution fetches the current secret directly from Privilege Cloud, ensuring that credential rotation schedules are respected automatically without requiring manual updates in RSA G&L.

Prerequisites​

Ensure you have the following before configuring the integration:

  • Administrative access to Idira Identity Administration and Privilege Cloud Safe management.
  • An active Idira Privilege Cloud tenant (qualified against version 15.0 or later).
  • RSA Governance & Lifecycle 8.0.0 Patch 10 or later.
  • Outbound HTTPS (TCP port 443) network connectivity from the RSA G&L server and any remote agents to both Idira Identity (https://<tenant-id>.id.cyberark.cloud) and Privilege Cloud (https://<subdomain>.privilegecloud.cyberark.cloud).

Idira Side Setup​

Configure Idira Privilege Cloud for OAuth-based API access by RSA G&L using least-privilege permissions.

info

This section is provided for reference. Work with your Idira administrator to ensure all configurations comply with enterprise security policies.

Manage space
├── Inventory → Identities → Users     (Step 2: Service User)
├── Inventory → Identities → Roles     (Step 3: Role Membership)
└── Policies  → Safes                  (Step 4: Dedicated Safe)

Privilege Cloud space
└── Accounts → Accounts & Requests → Accounts View (Step 5: Target Credential)

Step 1: Identify Tenant URLs and Login Suffix​

The plugin requires two tenant endpoints:

G&L Configuration FieldDescriptionFormat Example
Identity Tenant URLIdira Identity OAuth 2.0 token endpoint hosthttps://<tenant-id>.id.cyberark.cloud
Privilege Cloud URLPrivilege Cloud PVWA REST API hosthttps://<subdomain>.privilegecloud.cyberark.cloud
Discovering Tenant URLs

Both URLs can be determined using Idira platform discovery:

curl -s https://platform-discovery.cyberark.cloud/api/v2/services/subdomain/<subdomain>

Extract identity_administration.api for the Identity Tenant URL and pcloud.api (without a trailing slash) for the Privilege Cloud URL.

Note your login suffix (for example, cyberark.cloud.12345), visible under your username in the profile menu. The service user uses this same suffix.

Step 2: Create the Service User​

  1. Navigate to Manage → Inventory → Identities → Users and click Add User.

  2. Complete the Account details:
    • Login name: Enter a dedicated name (for example, svc_gl or svc_rsa_gl_pam).
    • Suffix: Ensure your tenant login suffix is selected. The full login@suffix becomes the Client ID.
    • Email address: Enter a monitored distribution list or team mailbox.
    • Display name: For example, RSA G&L Service Account.

  3. Set Password Type to Generated. Click Copy and store this generated password in your secure vault. This value becomes the Client Secret.

  4. Under Status, select Is OAuth confidential client. Idira automatically enables Is service user and Password never expires.

  5. Click Create User.

Record the generated credentials for RSA G&L:

  • Client ID: The full login name (for example, svc_gl@cyberark.cloud.12345)
  • Client Secret: The generated password

Step 3: Assign the Privilege Cloud Users Role​

  1. In the Manage space, navigate to Inventory → Identities → Roles.
  2. Search for Privilege Cloud Users.

  3. Open Privilege Cloud Users, select the Members tab, click Add, select the service user, and click Save.

Least Privilege

Do not assign the service user to Privilege Cloud Administrators, Safe Managers, or any other administrative role. The service user requires member access to Privilege Cloud Users only.

Step 4: Create a Dedicated Safe and Assign Permissions​

To isolate secrets accessed by RSA G&L, create a dedicated Safe.

  1. Navigate to Manage → Policies → Safes and click Create Safe.

  2. Define Safe Properties: Enter a Safe Name (for example, RSA-GL-Integration) and a description. Leave dual-control disabled.

  3. Select Safe Members: Search for and select the service user created in Step 2.

  4. Set Permissions: Under Access, select List accounts and Retrieve accounts. Clear Use accounts.

  5. Click Create Safe.
PermissionRequiredUsage
List accountsYesAccount lookup and connectivity validation
Retrieve accountsYesDecrypting and retrieving account passwords
Use accountsNoInteractive sessions (not required by RSA G&L)

Step 5: Store Target Credentials in Privilege Cloud​

Ensure the target account platform is active before adding credentials:

  1. Navigate to Manage → Policies → Account platforms. Select the platform group (for example, Cloud Service) and activate the required platform if needed.

  2. Switch to the Privilege Cloud space (Navigate ⋮⋮ → Privilege Cloud), go to Accounts → Accounts & Requests → Accounts View, and click Add account.

  3. Select the System type (for example, Cloud Service), the Platform, and select the dedicated Safe (RSA-GL-Integration).

  4. Enter the account properties:
    • Username: The account login or application client ID.
    • Address: Target host, domain, or directory ID (if applicable).
    • Password: The secret or password value.
    • Customize account name: Enter a unique name (for example, Entra-RSA-GL-Collector).

  5. Click Add.

Installation and Configuration in G&L​

note

Requires RSA Governance and Lifecycle 8.0.0 Patch 10 or later.

Complete the Idira Side Setup before proceeding. You will need the Privilege Cloud URL, Identity Tenant URL, Client ID, and Client Secret.

Step 1: Install the Plugin​

  1. Log in to the RSA G&L UI as a System Administrator.
  2. Navigate to Admin → System → Password Vault.
  3. Under Vault Types, click Upload New Vault Type.

  4. In the dialog, enter the details:
    • Vault Type Name: Idira-Privilege-Cloud
    • Description: Retrieves credentials from Idira Privilege Cloud using OAuth 2.0 client credentials.
    • JAR File: Click Choose File and select the distribution JAR (idira-privilegecloud-plugin-dist-1.0-<timestamp>.jar).

  5. Click OK. Idira-Privilege-Cloud appears in the Vault Types list.

note

After uploading a new vault type, restart all remote G&L agents to ensure they load the plugin.

Step 2: Configure the Password Vault​

  1. In the Password Vault Configuration section, select Idira-Privilege-Cloud from the dropdown and click + Create.

  2. Complete the configuration form:

    FieldDescriptionExample
    Privilege Cloud URLBase URL of your Privilege Cloud PVWA instancehttps://<subdomain>.privilegecloud.cyberark.cloud
    Identity Tenant URLBase URL of your Idira Identity Administration tenanthttps://<tenant-id>.id.cyberark.cloud
    Client IDService user login identifier including suffixsvc_gl@cyberark.cloud.12345
    Client SecretService user generated secret key (masked)••••••••••••••••

  3. Click Test Connection. A Connection successful status confirms token retrieval and API communication.

  4. Click OK to save. The saved configuration displays Edit and Test Connection options.

Step 3: Create Vault Profiles​

A vault profile maps a specific collector or connector credential to an account stored in an Idira Safe. Create one profile per managed account.

  1. Navigate to the Password Vault Profiles section and click + Create Profile.

  2. Fill in the profile fields:

    FieldDescriptionExample
    NameDisplay name for this profileEntra RSA G&L Collector
    DescriptionOptional descriptionMicrosoft Entra client secret
    Safe NameSafe where the credential is storedRSA-GL-Integration
    Account NameAccount Name or Username in Privilege CloudEntra-RSA-GL-Collector

  3. Click Test Profile. A Credential retrieved successfully response confirms the account was found and its password decrypted.

  4. Click OK to save. The profile appears in the list with the identifier formatted as Safe Name (Account Name).

Step 4: Use the Profile in a Collector or Connector​

In the collector or connector configuration, keep non-sensitive parameters static and reference the vault profile for the secret:

  1. Open the collector configuration (for example, Microsoft Entra ID).
  2. Enter the static Username or Application ID.
  3. For Password, select Use Password Vault → Existing Profile and choose your profile (Entra RSA G&L Collector).

  4. Click Test, then click Save.

RSA G&L retrieves the current password from Idira Privilege Cloud each time the collector or connector runs.

Known Limitations​

  • Client Credentials Only: The plugin uses the OAuth 2.0 client credentials grant for machine-to-machine authentication. User interactive authentication and authorization code grants are not supported.
  • Dual-Control Safes Not Supported: Safes requiring access approval return HTTP 403. G&L automated background retrieval cannot submit interactive access requests.
  • No Check-in / Checkout Locking: Passwords are retrieved on demand without exclusive checkout. Do not configure one-time-password or exclusive checkout policies for credentials used by RSA G&L.
  • Exact Account Matching: Privilege Cloud account searches return fuzzy matches. The plugin enforces an exact match against the Account Name first, then the Username within the specified Safe.
  • HTTPS Enforced: All endpoints require HTTPS. HTTP redirects are disabled to safeguard credentials.

Troubleshooting​

Authentication and Token Errors (HTTP 400)​

Error Message:

Idira Identity token exchange failed with status: 400 (access_denied: invalid client creds or client not allowed)

  • Root Cause: Invalid Client ID or Client Secret, or the service user is not configured as an OAuth confidential client.
  • Resolution:
    1. Verify the Client ID includes the full login suffix (for example, svc_gl@cyberark.cloud.12345).
    2. Confirm Is OAuth confidential client is selected for the service user in Idira Identity Administration.
    3. Reset the service user password in Idira Identity Administration with Require password change at next login cleared, update the secret in RSA G&L, and test the connection.

API Authorization and Role Membership (HTTP 401)​

Error Message:

Idira Accounts API returned error status: 401

  • Root Cause: The service user authenticated successfully but is not authorized to query Privilege Cloud APIs, or the Privilege Cloud URL is incorrect.
  • Resolution:
    1. Confirm the service user is a member of the Privilege Cloud Users role.
    2. Verify the Privilege Cloud URL matches https://<subdomain>.privilegecloud.cyberark.cloud without additional path elements such as /PasswordVault.

Account Lookup and Resolution​

Error Message:

No account was found for the provided SafeName and AccountName

  • Root Cause: The Safe Name or Account Name does not match any entry in Privilege Cloud, or the service user lacks list permissions on the Safe.
  • Resolution:
    1. Verify the Safe Name matches the Safe in Privilege Cloud exactly (case-insensitive).
    2. Confirm the Account Name matches either the custom account name or the account username.
    3. Ensure the service user has List accounts permissions on the Safe.

Error Message:

Multiple accounts found for the provided SafeName and AccountName

  • Root Cause: More than one account in the Safe has the same username or account name.
  • Resolution:
    1. In Privilege Cloud, assign a unique custom account name (for example, Entra-RSA-GL-Collector).
    2. Update the RSA G&L Vault Profile Account Name to specify that unique name.

Password Retrieval and Safe Permissions (HTTP 403 / 404)​

Error Message:

Idira denied immediate password retrieval (403)

  • Root Cause: The service user lacks retrieve permissions, or the Safe has dual-control workflow active.
  • Resolution:
    1. Verify the service user has Retrieve accounts permission on the Safe.
    2. Confirm dual-control approval is disabled on the Safe.

Error Message:

Idira account was not found during password retrieval (404)

  • Root Cause: The account was deleted or modified in Privilege Cloud between search lookup and password retrieval.
  • Resolution:
    1. Confirm the account exists in Privilege Cloud.
    2. Retest the profile in RSA G&L.

Network and TLS Connectivity​

Error Message:

Connectivity or parsing error during Idira Identity token exchange or Connectivity error with Idira Privilege Cloud API

  • Root Cause: Network egress restrictions, firewall blocking, proxy interference, or TLS inspection preventing HTTPS communication.
  • Resolution:
    1. Ensure outbound HTTPS (port 443) is open from the RSA G&L server and remote agents to *.id.cyberark.cloud and *.privilegecloud.cyberark.cloud.
    2. Ensure endpoint URLs begin with https://.
    3. Confirm intermediate TLS inspection proxies do not intercept or terminate connections without presenting trusted certificates.

Profile Configuration Mismatch​

Error Message:

Password vault profile is not an Idira Privilege Cloud profile

  • Root Cause: The profile was created under a different vault type.
  • Resolution:
    1. Create a new profile under the Idira-Privilege-Cloud vault configuration.
    2. Assign the new profile to the target collector or connector.

References​

Idira Identity Documentation

  • Add service users: Creating service users with OAuth confidential client authentication.
  • API token authentication for Idira Identity: OAuth 2.0 /oauth2/platformtoken endpoint reference.

Idira Privilege Cloud Documentation

  • Manage Safe members: Safe permissions and member assignment.
  • Add accounts: Creating and managing privileged accounts.
  • Microsoft Azure Application Keys platform: Platform configuration for application secrets.
  • Privilege Cloud REST APIs overview: PVWA REST API specifications.
  • Get accounts API: GET /API/Accounts search and filter parameters.
  • Get password value API: POST /API/Accounts/{id}/Password/Retrieve retrieval specifications.

Industry Standards

  • RFC 6749 Section 4.4: Client Credentials Grant: OAuth 2.0 framework specification.

entry.title: Keeper Enterprise
entry.summary: Keeper Enterprise is a zero-knowledge, end-to-end encrypted secrets management platform with privileged access management capabilities. It provides secure credential vaulting, just-in-time access, and password rotation for enterprise infrastructure across cloud, on-premises, and hybrid environments.Versions: 8.0.0 P10
entry.content:
Keeper Enterprise is a zero-knowledge, end-to-end encrypted secrets management platform with privileged access management capabilities. It provides secure credential vaulting, just-in-time access, and password rotation for enterprise infrastructure across cloud, on-premises, and hybrid environments.

Versions: 8.0.0 P10

Introduction​

This plugin integrates RSA Governance and Lifecycle (G&L) with Keeper Enterprise using the Keeper Secrets Manager (KSM) Java SDK. It retrieves credentials for use by collectors and connectors. Credentials are not cached; each retrieval fetches the current password directly from Keeper. All HTTPS transport and end-to-end encryption are handled by the KSM SDK.

Prerequisites​

Ensure you have the following:

  • Administrative access to your Keeper Enterprise vault.
  • The Keeper Secrets Manager CLI installed on a machine used to initialize credentials.
  • A list of managed accounts that RSA G&L will access.

Keeper Side Setup​

This section describes how to configure Keeper Enterprise for SDK-based access by RSA G&L.

info

This section is provided for reference only. Contact your Keeper administrator to configure Keeper Enterprise in line with your organization's security requirements.

Step 1: Create a Shared Folder​

Keeper Secrets Manager applications can only access Shared Folders. Regular folders are not visible to the SDK.

warning

Use Create New > Shared Folder (identified by a two-person icon). If you use Create New > Folder (plain folder), the KSM application will not see it. If the folder does not appear in Secrets Manager, delete it and recreate it as a Shared Folder.

  1. Log in to Keeper Vault at keepersecurity.com.

  2. Click Create New > Shared Folder.

  3. Complete the following fields and click Create.

    FieldValue
    Folder NameA descriptive name, for example AD Credentials
    User PermissionsNo User Permissions
    Record PermissionsView Only

Step 2: Create a Login Record​

  1. In My Vault, open the shared folder, click the folder menu (...), and select New Record.

  2. Select record type Login.

  3. Complete the following fields and click Save.

    FieldValue
    TitleA descriptive name for the account, for example AD Service Account
    LoginThe username
    PasswordThe credential password

Step 3: Note the Record UID​

The Record UID is the permanent identifier used by the plugin to locate a record. It does not change if the record is renamed or moved.

  1. Open the record in Keeper Vault.
  2. Click the record menu (...) at the top-right of the record panel and select Record Info.
  3. Copy the UID, a 22-character Base64 string, for example YSq-xxLdgsO2RJbz46EKkA.

This value is entered in the G&L vault profile as the Record UID.

Step 4: Create a KSM Application​

  1. In Keeper Vault, click Secrets Manager in the left sidebar.
  2. Click Create Application, enter a name (for example GL-PAM), and click Save.
  3. With the application selected, click the Folders and Records tab.
  4. Search for and select your shared folder. It is added with Read Only access.
  5. Click Save. The Records column should show a count greater than zero.

Step 5: Generate an Access Token and Initialize Credentials​

warning

One-time access tokens cannot be retrieved after generation. Copy the token before closing this dialog.

  1. With the application selected, click the Devices tab and click Add Device.

  2. Complete the following fields.

    FieldValue
    Device NameA descriptive name, for example GL-PAM-Plugin
    MethodOne-Time Access Token
    Lock external WAN IPLeave unchecked

  3. Click Generate Access Token and copy the token. The format is US:xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx.

  4. On any machine with the KSM CLI installed, run the following to exchange the token for permanent credentials.

    # Install the CLI (one-time setup)
    pip install keeper-secrets-manager-cli

    # Exchange the token to create keeper.ini in your home directory
    ksm profile init --token <YOUR_ONE_TIME_TOKEN>

  5. Open the generated keeper.ini file (%USERPROFILE%\keeper.ini on Windows, ~/keeper.ini on Linux/macOS).

    [_default]
    clientid          = <base64 string>
    privatekey        = <base64 string>
    appkey            = <base64 string>
    hostname          = keepersecurity.com
    appownerpublickey = <base64 string>
    serverpublickeyid = 10

    Each value maps directly to a field in the G&L vault configuration in the next section.

Installation and Configuration in G&L​

note

Requires RSA Governance and Lifecycle 8.0.0 Patch 10 or later.

Complete the Keeper Side Setup section before proceeding. You will need the values from the keeper.ini file generated in Step 5.

Step 1: Install the Plugin​

  1. Log in to the RSA G&L UI as a System Administrator.

  2. Open the Admin menu and click System.

  3. Click the Password Vault tab.

  4. Scroll to the Vault Types section and click Upload New Vault Type.

  5. Enter a Vault Type Name (for example, Keeper-Enterprise) and an optional description. Click Choose File, select the distribution JAR (keeper-enterprise-plugin-dist-1.0-<timestamp>.jar), and click OK.

    note

    After uploading, restart all remote G&L agents to load the new vault type.

  6. After the upload completes, Keeper-Enterprise appears in the Vault Types list.

Step 2: Configure the Password Vault​

  1. Scroll to the Password Vault Configuration section. Select Keeper-Enterprise from the dropdown and click + Create.

  2. Copy the values from keeper.ini into the corresponding fields, click Test Connection, and click OK to save.

    G&L Fieldkeeper.ini KeyDescription
    HostnamehostnameKeeper server hostname. Varies by region: keepersecurity.com (US), keepersecurity.eu (EU), keepersecurity.com.au (AU), keepersecurity.jp (JP), keepersecurity.ca (CA)
    Client IDclientidBase64-encoded application identity
    Private KeyprivatekeyBase64-encoded ECC private key (masked)
    App KeyappkeyBase64-encoded application encryption key (masked)
    App Owner Public KeyappownerpublickeyOptional but recommended
    Server Public Key IDserverpublickeyidDefaults to 10

  3. The saved configuration shows Edit, Test Connection, and Delete options. Use Test Connection at any time to verify connectivity.

Step 3: Create Vault Profiles​

A vault profile maps a G&L managed account to a specific record in Keeper by its UID. Create one profile per account.

  1. Navigate to the Password Vault Profiles section and click + Create Profile.

  2. Complete the following fields and click Test Profile. A Credential retrieved successfully response confirms the UID is valid and the password is accessible. Click OK to save.

    FieldDescriptionExample
    NameDisplay name for this profileActive Directory
    DescriptionOptional descriptionAD service account
    Record UIDThe 22-character Base64 UID copied in Step 3 of the Keeper Side SetupYSq-xxLdgsO2RJbz46EKkA

  3. The profile appears in the list. The Identifier column shows the Record UID.

  4. Repeat for each account that requires Keeper password retrieval.

  5. In G&L, open the collector or connector configuration, locate Use Password Vault, select the profile, click Test, and save.

Known Limitations​

  • Records are accessed by UID, not by title. Record UIDs are permanent and do not change if a record is renamed or moved. If a record is deleted and recreated, its UID changes and the vault profile must be updated.

  • The KSM application must have access to the record's Shared Folder. If the record is moved out of the shared folder that the KSM application can access, credential retrieval will fail. Verify folder membership in Keeper Vault under Secrets Manager > application > Folders and Records.

Troubleshooting​

Connection Errors​

  • Root Cause: Hostname region mismatch, incorrect vault configuration values from keeper.ini, or deactivated KSM application.
  • Resolution:
    1. Verify that all six vault configuration fields match the values in keeper.ini exactly.
    2. Confirm the Hostname matches your Keeper region (for example, keepersecurity.com or keepersecurity.eu).
    3. Verify that the KSM application is active and has not been deleted in Keeper Vault.

Record Not Found​

  • Root Cause: Invalid Record UID in the vault profile, or the record resides outside the KSM application shared folder.
  • Resolution:
    1. Confirm the Record UID in the vault profile matches the 22-character UID in Keeper.
    2. Verify the record is inside a Shared Folder that the KSM application has permission to access.
    3. In Keeper Vault, navigate to Secrets Manager → Folders and Records and verify the folder is listed with a record count greater than zero.

Access Denied Errors​

  • Root Cause: Insufficient permissions on the shared folder or the target record was moved or deleted.
  • Resolution:
    1. Verify the KSM application has Read Only access granted to the shared folder.
    2. Confirm the shared folder contains the target record and has not been removed.

References​

Keeper Security Documentation

  • Keeper Secrets Manager Overview: Architecture, zero-knowledge encryption, and access controls.
  • Keeper Secrets Manager CLI: Initializing profiles and exchanging one-time access tokens.
  • Keeper Secrets Manager Java SDK: Record retrieval methods and caching controls.
  • Keeper Security Regions and URLs: Regional API endpoints and hostnames.

entry.title: BeyondTrust Password Safe
entry.summary: BeyondTrust Password Safe is an enterprise solution for privileged account, credential, and secrets management. It automates password rotation, enforces strong security policies, monitors and audits privileged sessions, and manages access for human and machine identities across traditional, cloud, and DevOps environments.Versions: 8.0.0 P10
entry.content:
BeyondTrust Password Safe is an enterprise solution for privileged account, credential, and secrets management. It automates password rotation, enforces strong security policies, monitors and audits privileged sessions, and manages access for human and machine identities across traditional, cloud, and DevOps environments.

Versions: 8.0.0 P10

Introduction​

This plugin integrates RSA Governance and Lifecycle (G&L) with BeyondTrust Password Safe using the BeyondTrust REST API v3 and OAuth 2.0 authentication. It retrieves credentials for use by collectors and connectors. Credentials are not cached; each retrieval fetches the current password directly from BeyondTrust, so password rotation policies are respected automatically.

Prerequisites​

Before you begin, ensure you have the following:

  • Administrative access to your BeyondTrust Password Safe instance.
  • A list of managed accounts that RSA G&L will access.
  • The IP address or CIDR range of the RSA G&L instance for API access configuration.

Application Setup​

This section describes how to configure BeyondTrust Password Safe for OAuth-based API access by RSA G&L.

info

This section is provided for reference only. Contact your BeyondTrust administrator to configure BeyondTrust Password Safe in line with your organization's security requirements.

Step 1: Create a User Group and Smart Group​

  1. Create a User Group:

    1. Navigate to Configuration > Role Based Access > User Management.
    2. Click the Groups tab and select Create New Group > Create a New Group.
    3. Enter API Access as the Group Name, provide a Description, and click Create Group.

  2. Create a Smart Group:

    1. Navigate to Managed Accounts.
    2. Select the accounts RSA G&L will access.
    3. Click Add to Smart Group.
    4. In the Add To Manual Smart Group dialog, enter G&L in the Smart Group (manual) field.
    5. Click Add As New Option.

    6. Set Category to Managed Accounts, provide an optional Description, and click Add Selected Accounts To Smart Group.

Step 2: Configure API Access and Permissions​

  1. Configure an API Access Policy:

    1. Go to Configuration > General > API Registrations.
    2. Click Create API Registration and select API Access Policy.
    3. Fill in the registration details, including the Access Token Duration.

    4. Click Add Authentication Rule, select CIDR and IP Rule, and enter the CIDR range for your RSA G&L instance.
    5. Click Create Rule.

  2. Assign Permissions:

    1. Open the API Access group and select the Features tab.
    2. Select All Features, then search for and select Password Safe Account Management and Password Safe System Management.
    3. Click Assign Permissions and grant Read Only access.

Step 3: Create an Access Policy​

  1. Go to Configuration > Privileged Access Management Policies > Access Policies.
  2. Click Create Policy.
  3. Enter G&L API Auto Approve Policy as the Access Policy Name, provide a Description, and click Create Policy.

  4. On the Schedule tab, click Create Schedule.

  5. Enable All Day and verify the Recurrence settings.

  6. Under Policy Types, select View Password, Auto Approve, and API Only Access.

  7. Click Create Schedule.

Step 4: Assign Smart Group Roles​

  1. Go to User Management > Groups > API Access.
  2. Click the Smart Groups tab, find the G&L smart group, and select Edit Password Safe Roles.
  3. Select the Requestor role.
  4. For Access Policy, select G&L API Auto Approve Policy.

  5. Click Save Roles.

Step 5: Create an API User​

  1. Go to Configuration > Role Based Access > User Management.
  2. Click the Users tab and select Add an Application User.
  3. Enter svc_gl_pam as the Username.
  4. Under API Access Policy, select the policy you created.
  5. Copy and store the Client ID and Client Secret. These are required for the G&L configuration.

  6. Click Create User.
  7. Assign the user to the API Access group.

Step 6: Enable API Access on Managed Accounts​

  1. Go to Managed Accounts.
  2. For each account, set Enable API Access to Yes in the Account Settings.

Installation and Configuration in G&L​

note

Requires RSA Governance and Lifecycle 8.0.0 Patch 10 or later.

Complete the Application Setup section before proceeding. You will need the Client ID and Client Secret from Step 5.

Step 1: Install the Plugin​

  1. Log in to the RSA G&L UI as a System Administrator.

  2. Open the Admin menu and click System.

  3. Click the Password Vault tab.

  4. Scroll to the Vault Types section and click Upload New Vault Type.

  5. Enter a Vault Type Name (for example, BeyondTrust-Password-Safe) and an optional description. Click Choose File, select the distribution JAR (beyondtrust-password-safe-plugin-dist-1.0-<timestamp>.jar), and click OK.

    note

    After uploading, restart all remote G&L agents to load the new vault type.

  6. After the upload completes, BeyondTrust Password Safe appears in the Vault Types list.

Step 2: Configure the Password Vault​

  1. Scroll to the Password Vault Configuration section. Select BeyondTrust Password Safe from the dropdown and click + Create.

  2. Complete the following fields, click Test Connection, and click OK to save.

    FieldDescription
    Base URLBase URL of your BeyondTrust Password Safe instance (for example, https://instance.company.com)
    Client IDOAuth 2.0 Client ID from the registered BeyondTrust application
    Client SecretOAuth 2.0 Client Secret from the registered BeyondTrust application (masked)

  3. The saved configuration shows Edit, Test Connection, and Delete options. Use Test Connection at any time to verify connectivity.

Step 3: Create Vault Profiles​

A vault profile maps a G&L managed account to a Managed System and Account in BeyondTrust. Create one profile per account.

  1. Navigate to the Password Vault Profiles section and click + Create Profile.

  2. Complete the following fields and click Test Profile. A Credential retrieved successfully response confirms the account is reachable in BeyondTrust. Click OK to save.

    FieldDescriptionExample
    NameDisplay name for this profileOracle DB Admin
    DescriptionOptional descriptionOracle production DBA account
    System NameManaged System name exactly as it appears in BeyondTrust Password SafePROD-DB-01
    Account NameManaged Account name exactly as it appears in BeyondTrust Password Safeoracle_dba

  3. The profile appears in the list. The Identifier column shows System Name (Account Name).

  4. Repeat for each account that requires BeyondTrust password retrieval.

  5. In G&L, open the collector or connector configuration, locate Use Password Vault, select the profile, click Test, and save.

Known Limitations​

  • Fixed request duration. Each credential checkout is valid for 1 minute. If a checkout is still active when a new request is submitted for the same account, BeyondTrust returns a 409 Conflict error. Wait for the active request to expire and retry, or manually check in the request from the BeyondTrust Password Safe UI.
  • Double-quote characters in passwords. Double-quote characters are removed from retrieved passwords. If an account password contains double quotes, update the password in BeyondTrust to use a different special character.

Troubleshooting​

API Authentication Errors​

  • Root Cause: Invalid Client ID or Client Secret, unassigned API user group, or unauthorized source IP address.
  • Resolution:
    1. Verify that the Client ID and Client Secret match the application user credentials.
    2. Confirm that the API user is assigned to the API Access user group.
    3. Confirm that the API access policy CIDR range includes the IP address of the RSA G&L instance and all remote agents.

Unable to Retrieve Passwords​

  • Root Cause: Missing role assignment on the smart group, approval schedule requirement, or API access disabled on accounts.
  • Resolution:
    1. Confirm that the Requestor role is assigned to the G&L smart group.
    2. Verify that the access policy is configured to auto-approve requests across all hours.
    3. Confirm that API access is enabled on the managed accounts in BeyondTrust Account Settings.

Access Denied Errors​

  • Root Cause: Missing feature permissions for the user group.
  • Resolution:
    1. Verify that the API Access user group has Read Only permissions granted for both Password Safe Account Management and Password Safe System Management.
